title: Amazon Redshift Data Warehousing
summary: Columnar analytics at scale: distribution and sort keys, concurrency scaling, Spectrum and zero-ETL.
tldr: **Redshift** is the columnar, massively parallel data warehouse for complex SQL over TBs to PBs. Move BI and aggregation queries here instead of loading the OLTP database.

Tune with **distribution style** (co-locate join keys, `ALL` for small dimensions) and **sort keys** (on the column you filter by, usually a date). Add **concurrency scaling** and **materialized views** for bursts of repeated dashboard queries.
Avoid ETL with **zero-ETL** from Aurora, RDS and DynamoDB; query S3 in place with **Spectrum**; give teams isolated compute over the same data with **data sharing**.

keyFacts.text: Distribution styles. **KEY** on the join column co-locates matching rows; **ALL** copies a small table to every node. Both cut data redistribution during joins.
Rows stored in sort-key order let Redshift skip blocks outside a filter range, so a `sale_date` sort key turns full scans into small range reads.
**Redshift Serverless** bills in Redshift Processing Unit-hours only while queries run. Set a **base capacity** for performance and **usage limits** to cap spend.
**Concurrency scaling** adds transient clusters for queued read queries; a cluster earns up to one hour of free concurrency-scaling credit per day.
**Aurora zero-ETL** keeps Redshift copies of Aurora tables within seconds of the source, with no pipeline to build and little load on the database.

keywords.cue: complex aggregations over TBs slow the RDS database
joins shuffle data between nodes, full scans on date filter
keywords.answer: KEY distribution on the join column, sort key on the date

keywords.cue: Monday-morning dashboard queue, same expensive aggregations
keywords.answer: Concurrency scaling + materialized views with auto refresh

keywords.cue: seconds-fresh Aurora data in Redshift, no ETL pipeline
join Redshift with Parquet history in S3, don't load it
teams need isolated compute on the same live data, no copies
keywords.answer: Data sharing to Redshift Serverless workgroups

keywords.cue: ad hoc queries a few hours a month on a 24/7 cluster

traps: Redshift has no "read replica"; scale reads with concurrency scaling, data sharing or a bigger cluster.
Separate WLM queues prioritize workloads on one cluster but don't give teams isolated compute or separate billing.
Distributing a fact table on a date column skews data and doesn't help joins on customer ID.
Resizing the cluster every week for a predictable peak is high effort; concurrency scaling does it automatically.
Spectrum queries S3 in place; DMS or COPY into the cluster is wrong when the requirement is "don't load the data".
